doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Professional at eleven on WSPD radio with the Swing Buddies
summary: He earned $125 a week at eleven singing on WSPD Toledo with a vocal quartet that protected him.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: By age 11 you were performing on the radio. I have a quote that said that – it’s quoting you – it says, “I was a pro at age 11.”
Yeah. Oh yeah. I was making $125 a week. That was about $10,000 a week today.
It was a lot of money.
Sure. I was a rich kid.
I bet you were. A singer, and rich. I bet you had all the girls, too.
Oh yeah. I didn’t know what to do with them, but I had them.
What was the context? In what time of day did you perform?
I was with another group of guys. We were called the Swing Buddies. It was four guys – three men and me – because I was really a kid. They used to take care of me

very well. Like when they went to have a drink, they never did it around me. When they went to have whatever else they had, like cigarettes with no names on them, they never did that around me. I was very well protected. It amazes me now how people can do what they do around children, and even now they dispense stuff like that to children. It’s amazing.
